title: UC Santa Barbara Researchers Join Three NSF Quantum Leap Challenge Institutes Under $290 Million Portfolio Renewal - Quantum Computing Report
author: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
text:
Faculty members from the University of California, Santa Barbara (UCSB) have been selected to participate across three centers within the National Science Foundation’s (NSF) Quantum Leap Challenge Institutes (QLCI) program. The initiative represents a nationwide $290 million funding allocation under the National Quantum Initiative Act framework, establishing and renewing eight QLCI centers (five expanded renewals and three newly created institutes) with individual 5-year awards ranging from $28 million to $37.5 million.

The QLCI framework spans 36 higher education institutions across 19 states, integrating academic researchers with Department of Energy (DOE) national laboratories, Department of Defense research units, NIST, and over 30 private quantum industry partners to accelerate the transition of fundamental physical research into scaled manufacturing.

Beyond hardware fabrication and algorithm development, the QLCI network mandates integrated workforce pipelines, combining doctoral research fellowships with community college training, K-12 outreach, and corporate internship programs to expand the U.S. quantum engineering talent pipeline.
